blocks.text: Jesus’ statement, “I am the true vine,” functions as a symbolic description within John’s portrayal of him and should be read in its immediate setting rather than treated as an isolated formula. The image binds together dependence on Jesus, fruit-bearing, pruning, love, obedience, friendship, joy, and being sent. It should not be used to defend abusive exclusion or to imply that suffering proves a leader’s right to harm others. The closing promise of the Spirit of truth adds a related emphasis: the Spirit testifies to Jesus, while the disciples also bear witness. Readers differ over how these sayings relate to later theological formulations, so their distinct contexts should be kept in view.
